paper_title: Early Detection of Performance Regressions by Bridging Local Performance Data and Architectural Models

selection.note: mineru key is unreliable; blocks are selected by title/body/inheritance. rescued_from_other counts sections labeled other but treated as typed roles.

claims.statement: The proposed approach can effectively detect end-to-end system performance regressions from local performance deviations with different intensities.
claims.evidence_quote: our approach can effectively detect system performance regressions with different intensities of local performance deviations

claims.statement: The proposed approach can detect regressions as early as the development phase, before full system performance testing is available.
claims.evidence_quote: our approach can detect regressions as early as in the development phase, in contrast to existing approaches that require the system to be fully built and deployed

claims.statement: Significant local performance deviations do not always cause system-level performance regressions, and the approach avoids false alarms in fixed-workload cases without system regressions.
claims.evidence_quote: Our approach does not generate false alarms when there is local performance deviation but no system performance regression.

claims.statement: Under various workloads, the approach maintains effectiveness: TeaStore is consistent with system testing in seven out of nine cases, and TrainTicket model predictions align except for an undetectable L1 case.
claims.evidence_quote: for TeaStore, our approach maintains consistency with the performance testing results in seven out of nine cases

overall_conclusion: The proposed approach bridges component-level performance deviation detection and architectural models to infer system-level performance regressions early in the development phase. Across TeaStore and TrainTicket benchmarks, fixed-workload evaluations show that the approach detects most injected regressions while avoiding false alarms in no-regression cases, and various-workload evaluations show maintained consistency in most cases.
comparable_notes: The comparison uses open-source systems TeaStore and TrainTicket, injected regressions at L1-L3, Low/Medium/High intensities, component-level tests repeated 30 times, system performance tests run 15 minutes with 5-minute warm-up and repeated 3 times, and regression outcomes derived from response time effect size and CPU MPD differences.
